answers.answer: No helper takes an argument. For a train that is running now, use the {hypetrain.*} helpers, such as level, progress, goal, remaining, percent, bar, total, timeLeft and topContributor. For the train that fired a Hype train starts or Hype train ends event response, use the {hype_train.*} helpers: level, total, goal and id. In a Hype train ends response, use only the {hype_train.*} helpers.

Before you start, you need a Twitch channel. The live helpers only show something while a train runs. The {hype_train.*} helpers work only in an event response for Hype train starts or Hype train ends, or in a pipeline one of those events started. All of this is in the section Before you use them.
answers.quote: A hype train is a Twitch feature, so these helpers read your Twitch channel only.

answers.answer: The spelling tells the two kinds apart: hypetrain without an underscore reads the train running now, and hype_train with an underscore carries the numbers of the event. You know it worked when the reply shows numbers instead of the braces as written. The !train example shows a sample output to compare against.
answers.quote: There are two kinds of hype train helper, and the spelling tells them apart.

answers.answer: To name a participant, put {hypetrain.topContributor} in a Hype train starts event response, for example next to {hype_train.level}. It works there because the train is still running. It does not work in a Hype train ends response, because by then the train no longer runs. For the chat command, use the live helpers such as {hypetrain.level}, {hypetrain.bar}, {hypetrain.remaining} and {hypetrain.timeLeft}, inside an {if.hypetrain.isActive:...|...} wrapper so the command still has a sentence when no train runs.
